payload.problem_addressed: Automating industrial CAD design and manufacturing requires a multimodal foundation model that can read engineering drawings and 3D geometry screenshots and write correct parametric-modelling scripts and Windows COM API code, across parts and assemblies.
payload.method_summary: Build IndustryForge-27B on top of Qwen3.5-VL-27B by curating six industrial-CAD sub-corpora (~52k multimodal samples: CAD-VQA, text2cadquery, text2cadquery-assembly, and COM sub-corpora for Inventor/SolidWorks: com_2d/com_3d/com_assembly) and training with a unified multi-task SFT recipe.
payload.contributions_summary: The authors introduce IndustryForge-27B, a domain-enhanced multimodal foundation model for industrial CAD built on Qwen3.5-VL-27B via multi-task SFT over six curated industrial-CAD corpora. It substantially outperforms the base model and a strong closed-source model (GPT-5.4) on CAD-domain benchmarks while retaining general capability, and is positioned as a shared substrate for downstream industrial-agent systems spanning CAD design to closed-loop self-improvement.
key_architecture_choices: Unified multi-task SFT recipe across six curated industrial-CAD sub-corpora
datasets: com_2d / com_3d / com_assembly (Inventor / SolidWorks COM API corpora)
metrics: Four CAD-domain benchmarks (percentage-point lift over base model)
payload.headline_results: +33.65pp average lift over the base model across four CAD-domain benchmarks, outperforming GPT-5.4 on all four; +1.56pp mean improvement across eleven general-capability benchmarks with no catastrophic forgetting.
claimed_advantages: Outperforms a strong closed-source model (GPT-5.4) on CAD-domain benchmarks
No catastrophic forgetting of general capabilities after CAD-domain SFT
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The paper's core recipe -- curating a corpus that pairs CAD geometry/drawings with correct parametric-modelling program code (text2cadquery) and multi-task SFT to produce a model that reliably emits valid CAD program syntax -- is directly analogous to hexgen's task of mapping B-rep graphs to valid hex-meshing DSL programs. Their CAD-VQA and text2cadquery corpora construction methodology could inform how we synthesize/augment (B-rep, program) training pairs or evaluate structural validity of generated CAD code at larger scale, even though their approach uses a large general-purpose VLM rather than a small graph-transformer with pointer heads.
payload.reviewer_notes: Only the abstract was available for extraction; architectural and training details (loss functions, exact validity-checking mechanism, whether generated code is verified against a compiler/checker) are not described here and would need the full paper to assess concretely transferable mechanisms versus scale-driven gains from a 27B-parameter base model.

payload.problem_addressed: LLMs are strong at code generation but lack mechanisms to reliably produce protocol refinements with correct behaviour (e.g. deadlock freedom), while formal specification approaches like multiparty session types (MPST) give rigorous guarantees but limited support for automatically constructing refinements.
payload.method_summary: Syntropy synthesizes protocol refinements guided by MPST specifications and LLMs, incorporating refinement constraints directly into the generation process so that generated variants provably satisfy correctness guarantees (deadlock freedom, compatibility).
payload.contributions_summary: The authors present Syntropy, a framework that combines LLM-based code generation with multiparty-session-type (MPST) specifications to synthesize deadlock-free communication protocol refinements. By embedding the refinement constraints directly into the generation process, Syntropy achieves 95.6%-99.5% validity while maintaining high syntactic correctness, and produces diverse, non-trivial refinements across multiple LLMs.
key_architecture_choices: Refinement constraints from multiparty session type (MPST) specifications incorporated directly into the LLM generation process
payload.headline_results: Syntropy achieves 95.6%-99.5% validity while maintaining high syntactic correctness, and produces diverse, non-trivial refinements across multiple LLMs.
claimed_advantages: High validity rate (95.6%-99.5%) of generated refinements against formal correctness guarantees
Works across multiple LLMs, not tied to one model
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The central mechanism -- incorporating formal specification constraints (here MPST guarantees) directly into the LLM generation process to push structural/behavioral validity rates into the 95%+ range -- is a directly transferable pattern for hexgen's structural-validity problem: constraining or guiding the autoregressive decoder's generation process with the same machine-checkable rules used by our frozen verifier (compiles, zero inverted elements, etc.) rather than only screening after the fact with best-of-N sampling. Their evaluation methodology (validity rate + syntactic correctness + diversity of valid outputs) is also a useful template for reporting hexgen's own generation quality.
payload.reviewer_notes: Only the abstract was available; the exact mechanism by which refinement constraints are 'incorporated directly into the generation process' (e.g. constrained decoding, iterative repair, verifier-guided resampling) is not specified here and matters a great deal for how directly this transfers to hexgen's decoder -- would need the full paper to determine if this is grammar-constrained decoding, post-hoc filtering, or an LLM-agent repair loop.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Multiparty session types (MPST) formal specification framework

provenance.problem_addressed: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation and program synthesis, yet lack mechanisms to reliably produce outputs with correct behaviour.
provenance.method_summary: It incorporates refinement constraints directly into the generation process, ensuring the generated variants satisfy these guarantees.
provenance.contributions_summary: Our comprehensive evaluation indicates that Syntropy achieves 95.6%-99.5% validity while maintaining high syntactic correctness, and produces diverse, non-trivial refinements across multiple LLMs.

payload.impact_rationale: Shows multi-task SFT on curated CAD-code corpora yields high-validity CAD program generation at scale, but most of the reported gain likely comes from base-model scale (27B VLM) rather than a specific mechanism we could isolate.
payload.effort_rationale: Adopting their corpus-curation + multi-task SFT recipe would mean building CAD-code corpora and a large VLM training pipeline, a substantial departure from hexgen's small graph-transformer architecture.

payload.impact_rationale: Embedding correctness constraints directly into the generation process (rather than post-hoc filtering) pushed structural validity to 95-99%, directly bearing on hexgen's top-priority structural-validity problem.
payload.effort_rationale: Would require designing an analogous constraint-injection mechanism tied to our frozen verifier's checks into the decoder's generation loop, a moderate project beyond current best-of-N screening.
